positions.thesis: ExxonMobil is the direct beneficiary of the US-Iran military exchange, which has driven Brent crude from ~$70 to $96+ per barrel. With the Strait of Hormuz at risk and supply disruption fears elevated, XOM upstream earnings will surge; the stock is already outperforming (+1.1%) on a broad down day, confirming relative strength. The geopolitical risk premium is likely to remain embedded for at least several days as the conflict shows no sign of de-escalating.

Vistra's nuclear and gas baseload assets are uniquely positioned to capture the AI data center power demand boom via signed 20-year PPAs with Meta and AWS; Q1 2026 revenue beat consensus with EBITDA guidance of $6.8-7.6B reaffirmed. At $160 versus analyst median targets of $230-293, the stock is significantly undervalued, and the current energy supply shock from geopolitical tensions further elevates power prices, adding a near-term catalyst to a strong structural thesis.
